Layer your anti-air defenses. Each anti-aircraft unit is optimized for a different range. A balanced mix of air defense systems will be key in controlling a battlefield's airspace.
Position your units well when attacking. Main battle tanks spearhead the assault. Following closely behind are lighter units, such as IFVs with infantry and other support units.
Plan your airstrikes. Send SEAD planes first to disrupt anti-aircraft defenses. Follow up with fighter-bombers and bombers. Keep fighters ready to counter enemy interceptors.
Reverse when falling back. Using the Reverse (G) order keeps a vehicle's front facing the enemy, exposing only the most heavily armored part.
Move your infantry carefully. Infantry squads are less accurate when advancing. Keep this in mind while attacking enemy positions.
Deploy your units on roads. The Move Fast (F) order lets vehicles travel as quickly as possible to their destination using the road network.
Use armed transports to support your infantry attacks. These vehicles, from APCs to IFVs, can provide suppressive fire for your assaulting soldiers.
Pay close attention to enemy fire. An enemy position can be spotted by keeping an eye out for missile smoke or tracers. Artillery is a great counter.
Deactivate your radar. Disable an air defense system's radar in the unit's Info Panel when an enemy SEAD is spotted. Anti-radiation missiles home in on active radar.
Switch off weapons when needed. A unit's weapon can be deactivated and reactivated by clicking on it in the unit's Info Panel.
Use height to your advantage. Hills and tall buildings offer better line of sight. Larger buildings also offer more protection compared to normal buildings.
Assault with the right weapons. Explosives, flamethrowers, and thermobaric weapons are limited in range but very effective in close combat.
Use Active Pause. In single-player, you can give orders to your units while using Active Pause. You can also change the game speed to suit your playstyle.
Use the Line of Sight tool. Check what your units can see with Line of Sight (C). Very useful when planning an attack or to spot potential ambush sites on the map.
Manage your units with Smart Orders. The AI will control your troops with customizable behavior. Smart Orders are a great way to reduce your micromanagement.
Take advantage of shared vision. Recon units spot enemy targets. Tanks and artillery with limited visibility use this intel to engage targets they can otherwise not see.
Lock the camera to a moving unit. Use the scroll wheel while hovering over a unit's label to lock the camera.
Watch replays. These are a great way to improve your skills. Recordings of past battles show all moves and unit deployments. Replays can be found under Saves in the Solo menu.
Relocate artillery often. Move artillery between salvos. This is a key tactic to avoid destruction through counter-battery fire.
Watch your Command Points. This is your income and lets you deploy units. Some more expensive units might require you to save up Command Points.
Deploy smoke. Smoke screens are an important way to mask units. They can be used to cover an attack or retreat across open terrain.
Use combined arms. Individual units are vulnerable. Combined arms, with mutual support between ground units, artillery, helicopters, and aircraft, is key to victory.
Keep the initiative. Don't sit on a captured Command Zone. Keep scouting the surrounding terrain and establish a defense in depth.
Deploy anti-aircraft units. Always keep one or multiple air defense systems near friendly forces. You never know when enemy helicopters or aircraft might strike.
Flank the enemy. This kind of attack can be especially devastating to those caught unaware.  Deploy recon units to scout potential routes or to warn against enemy attempts.
Deploy supply units. These are critical in keeping your forces in the fight. Supply units can restore damaged units, including infantry, and resupply units out of ammo and fuel.
Deploy defensive smoke. Armored vehicles, such as tanks and IFVs, can deploy defensive smoke (B) in an emergency. This breaks line of sight, especially useful against ATGM attacks.
Take care of your most expensive units. They might be powerful, but used without the proper support, are very vulnerable.
Use Command units. They increase the Veterancy of nearby forces by one level, boosting their efficiency in combat. Command units can also capture Command Zones.
Change altitude for helicopters. You can order helicopters to reduce altitude when in flight. This might conceal them from enemy anti-aircraft units or exploit the terrain.
Organize your advance during deployment. Place your units according to a plan and issue orders. They will execute orders automatically when the battle starts.
Recon corrects artillery fire. Artillery can benefit from a recon unit's "corrected fire" area of effect. Artillery will be more accurate on a target within this range.
Stop a unit in need of resupply. A unit must be stationary and not engaged in combat. Only then it can be repaired or resupplied by a nearby supply unit.
Capture unarmed units. A unit can capture an unarmed unit or structure if no other combat units are nearby. This applies to transports, supply units, and Forward Operating Bases.
Sides are automatically balanced. If one team has fewer players than the opposing team, its income and deck size will be increased to compensate.
Speed up your deployment. When creating a deck, create Combat Groups. These groupings of units will save time during the Deployment Phase of the battle.
Anticipate the enemy. If you know when and where an enemy might attack, spoil their plan by launching a pre-emptive artillery bombardment.
Communication is key. When playing multiplayer, talk to your team. Use beacons on the map to signal specific requests. Be ready to support team members in need.
Keep your guard up. If a position seems easy to defend, the enemy will likely favor an attack elsewhere.
Establish a reserve force. Keeping units in reserve behind the front lets you respond to enemy actions with flexibility. You can also easily rotate damaged units.
Be aware of a unit's strength. A unit will not engage if it is not powerful enough to damage the enemy target.
Take a unit's speed into account. Some units are faster than others. When moving a group of units, ensure all arrive at the same time.
Define your Rules of Engagements. These are behaviors that will set the way your units act and react on the battlefield. Take time to set these up.
Know when to unload. Make sure to unload infantry before your transports are exposed to enemy fire. Plan movement using Unload at Position (Y). In an emergency, hit Unload (U).
Know your range. A unit might carry different weapons, each with a different range. These can be checked in the Line of Sight tool (C) while the unit is selected.
Spread out. Space out your units on the front line. Don’t let them bunch up. This will minimize casualties in the case of airstrikes or artillery fire.
Know when to fire. Units are not only spotted by sight, but also sound. A unit opening fire will be noticed very quick. Holding fire is an effective tactic to remain hidden.
Switch between units. If several units are selected, switch between them (TAB). This lets you give each unit a different order while maintaining the selection.
Cancel orders. You can cancel (E) an order given to a unit at any time.
Queue orders. By holding (SHIFT) key, you can queue orders. Units will follow them sequentially. This is great when planning complex maneuvers or artillery fire.
